result.name: define_graph
result.description:
Replaces the open texture graph with a whole new one: graph is the body of a .texgraph file, as JSON (patina holds one graph per session). It clears the snapshot stack (push_snapshot) and the graph's path (save gives it one). A graph with faults is still taken, so edit_graph can fix it; save refuses it until it has none. A graph is {"version": 1, "size": S, "seed": N, "nodes": {id: node}}: version 1, or 2 for exposed parameters and input and graph nodes; size is the size the images are evaluated at, a power of two from 32 to 8192 (32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 or 8192); seed, 0 to 4294967295, is added to every noise's own seed, so the same graph gives the same pixels on every run. Ids and port names are [a-z][a-z0-9_]*. A node is {"type": T, "inputs": {port: source}, "params": {name: value}}, inputs and params left out when empty; a source is another node's id ("id.port" for a type with several outputs); a parameter left out takes its default. A value is a number, a string, or a list of numbers or of colours ([0, 0.5, 1], ["#202020", "#c0a080"]). Everything is image-relative and tiles. The images are the output nodes', at least one: one per role (base_colour, normal, roughness, metallic, occlusion, height), or a name ([a-z][a-z0-9_]*) in place of a role for an extra image <name>.png, such as a mask. metallic is packed into roughness.png's blue channel, so it needs a roughness output too. A fault names the node and the port or parameter it is on, and what would be right (the types, the ids, the range). The node types (nodes gives each one's inputs, outputs, parameters with ranges and defaults, and a worked example; nodes {"type": "tiles"} gives one): blend (combine two by a mode); blur (a wrapping blur); colour (a flat colour); distance (distance to a mask's edge); fbm (fractal noise); gradient (a ramp); gradient_map (colour a greyscale through stops); graph (another .texgraph as a node); height_to_normal (a normal from a height); input (an image input of this graph); levels (remap a range); mesh_curvature (curvature of the mesh (stand-in)); mesh_mask (a mesh group or material (stand-in)); mesh_occlusion (occlusion of the mesh (stand-in)); mesh_position (position on the mesh (stand-in)); noise (value noise); output (one of the material's images); shape (a shape per cell); stripes (stripes); tiles (tiles or bricks); transform (move, repeat, mirror, turn, scale); warp (bend by another image); worley (cells and their edges).
A graph that is not a .texgraph body (a missing or unknown key, a value of the wrong kind, a version other than 1 or 2, a bad size or seed) is refused, naming what is wrong, and the open graph is unchanged. Returns one line: the open graph's nodes, size and seed, then its faults, one a line.
Worked example, a tone per stave (eight staves across u, one random grey each) on a wood colour:
define_graph {"graph":{"version":1,"size":256,"seed":0,"nodes":{"wood":{"type":"colour","params":{"colour":"#aa7040"}},"tone":{"type":"noise","params":{"cells":[8,1],"interpolation":"step"}},"base":{"type":"blend","inputs":{"a":"wood","b":"tone"},"params":{"mode":"multiply"}},"out":{"type":"output","inputs":{"in":"base"},"params":{"role":"base_colour"}}}}}
returns: define_graph: the open graph is now 4 nodes, size 256, seed 0; no faults: it evaluates
The same with out's input misspelt as "bsae" is taken, and returns:
define_graph: the open graph is now 4 nodes, size 256, seed 0; 1 fault:
- node 'out' input 'in': names 'bsae', which is not a node; the nodes are base, out, tone, wood
Next: edit_graph to change it, get_graph to read it back, save to keep it.

graph.description: The whole graph, as a .texgraph file holds it: {"version": 1, "size": 256, "seed": 0, "nodes": {id: {"type": ..., "inputs": {...}, "params": {...}}}}.

result.name: nodes
result.description:
Lists patina's node types, the parts of a texture graph: for each, what it does, its inputs (optional ones marked), its outputs when it has several (a source names one as "id.port"), every parameter with its kind, range and default, and a worked define_graph example, run as written by patina's tests. Takes type (optional): one type's name for its entry alone; without it, every type's, in the order define_graph's description lists them. Changes nothing, and needs no open graph. Refused: a type patina has not (the error lists the types). Read it before writing a graph: define_graph's description carries only the types' names.
Worked example: nodes {"type":"stripes"} returns:
- stripes: greyscale stripes, 1 on a stripe: count whole stripes across the image, axis u (upright stripes), v (lying stripes) or diagonal (count along each axis), width a part of a period, softness the edge ramp's reach each side of the edge as a part of a period (the ramp is twice it); a stripe is centred on each multiple of 1/count. Inputs: none. Params: count: a whole number from 1 to 4096, default 8; axis: one of u, v, diagonal, default "u"; width: a number from 0 to 1, default 0.5; softness: a number from 0 to 0.5, default 0.
Worked example, 16 soft lying stripes:
define_graph {"graph":{"version":1,"size":256,"seed":0,"nodes":{"weft":{"type":"stripes","params":{"count":16,"axis":"v","width":0.4,"softness":0.2}},"out":{"type":"output","inputs":{"in":"weft"},"params":{"role":"base_colour"}}}}}
returns: define_graph: the open graph is now 2 nodes, size 256, seed 0; no faults: it evaluates

type.description: One node type's name, such as tiles; leave it out for every type.

result.name: edit_graph
result.description:
Edits the open graph by a list of operations, applied in order and all or nothing: when any operation cannot be applied, or the list would leave a fault the graph did not have, nothing changes and the result says why (the operation by number, or the new faults, each naming its node and port or parameter). Faults the graph already had (an opened file's, say) do not stop an edit, so they can be fixed one list at a time; the result lists those left. operations is an array of objects, each with op and its own keys:
- set_node {node, type, inputs, params}: adds the node, or replaces it whole (inputs and params optional, as in define_graph).
- remove_node {node}: removes it; disconnect or reconnect what reads it in the same list, or that is a new fault.
- connect {node, port, from}: sets node's input port to read from (an id, or "id.port"), replacing what it read.
- disconnect {node, port}: leaves the input unconnected (a fault unless the port is optional).
- set_params {node, params}: merges params into the node's, replacing those it names and keeping the rest.
- set {size, seed}: the graph's size or seed or both.
- set_parameter {name, value, drives, min, max}: adds the exposed parameter name, or changes the keys given. drives is a list of node parameters, each "node.param", all of one kind (a number, a whole number, a choice, two whole numbers or a colour; not a list); the parameter takes the narrowest range of them (the intersection, or an enum's common choices), narrowed again by min and max (numbers; null clears one), and every driven parameter takes its value, its own value in its node left out. A new parameter needs value and drives. A node parameter a parameter stops driving keeps the parameter's value as its own.
- remove_parameter {name}: removes it; the parameters it drove keep its value as their own.
- set_parameters {values}: sets parameters' values by name, such as {"mortar": 0.08}.
A value out of a parameter's range is a new fault (parameters['mortar']: is 0.5, but must be a number from 0 to 0.45), so the list is refused. get_graph lists the parameters; swatch and export take them for one call without editing the graph.
For example {"op":"set_params","node":"tone","params":{"seed":3}} gives tone another seed, {"op":"disconnect","node":"grained","port":"b"} on its own is refused (a blend's b is required), and {"op":"set","size":512,"seed":7} doubles the size and changes the seed. A list parameter (a gradient_map's positions or colours) is given whole, an array of numbers or of strings as define_graph reads it, and replaces the list; when the count changes, give both lists in one operation. Types, ports and parameters are define_graph's. Returns one line: what each operation did, then the graph's nodes, size, seed and faults.
Worked example, on define_graph's worked graph: a grain along v, multiplied in at 0.3:
edit_graph {"operations":[{"op":"set_node","node":"grain","type":"noise","params":{"cells":[64,2],"octaves":2}},{"op":"set_node","node":"grained","type":"blend","inputs":{"a":"base","b":"grain"},"params":{"mode":"multiply","opacity":0.3}},{"op":"connect","node":"out","port":"in","from":"grained"}]}
returns: edit_graph: 3 operations applied: added 'grain' (noise); added 'grained' (blend); connected 'out' input 'in' to 'grained' (was 'base'). The graph is 6 nodes, size 256, seed 0; no faults: it evaluates
Then edit_graph {"operations":[{"op":"remove_node","node":"tone"}]} changes nothing and returns:
edit_graph: nothing changed: the operations would leave 1 new fault:
- node 'base' input 'b': names 'tone', which is not a node; the nodes are base, grain, grained, out, wood

operations.description: The operations, applied in order, all or nothing: each an object with op (set_node, remove_node, connect, disconnect, set_params, set, set_parameter, remove_parameter or set_parameters) and its keys.

result.name: get_graph
result.description:
Reads back the open graph: a line with its nodes, size, seed, path (the file save last wrote or open read, or no path) and faults, one a line, each naming its node and port or parameter; then the graph exactly as save would write it, a .texgraph file: version, size, seed, then one node a line in id order, inputs and params in name order, the parameters the graph gives (a default it leaves out is not written). Give that JSON back to define_graph as graph to start again from it. Takes nothing, and changes nothing. A graph with exposed parameters (version 2, set with edit_graph's set_parameter) lists them between the two, a line each: its name, kind, value, range (the narrowest of the node parameters it drives) and what it drives; and in the file each driven node parameter shows {"driven_by": "<name>"} where its own value would be, which save leaves out and define_graph reads back. A graph using others as graph nodes (T-140) lists each after those, a line each: the file its path resolved to (against the graph's own file's folder, or the tool folder for a graph never saved, which the head line says), the nested graph's parameters with the values set on the node and their ranges, its inputs (name and kind, and whether it has a default) and its outputs as the node's ports (wall.base_colour). For samples/graphs/bricks.texgraph the lines are:
parameters (3):
- jitter: a number, 0.25, from 0 to 1; drives layout.jitter
- mortar: a number, 0.1, from 0 to 0.45; drives layout.gap
- tint: a colour, "#a8452f", any colour "#rrggbb"; drives clay.colour
and its layout node reads "gap": { "driven_by": "mortar" }.
Worked example, after define_graph's worked example, get_graph {} returns:
get_graph: 4 nodes, size 256, seed 0; no path (save gives it one); no faults: it evaluates
{
  "version": 1,
  "size": 256,
  "seed": 0,
  "nodes": {
    "base": { "type": "blend", "inputs": { "a": "wood", "b": "tone" }, "params": { "mode": "multiply" } },
    "out": { "type": "output", "inputs": { "in": "base" }, "params": { "role": "base_colour" } },
    "tone": { "type": "noise", "params": { "cells": [8, 1], "interpolation": "step" } },
    "wood": { "type": "colour", "params": { "colour": "#aa7040" } }
  }
}

result.name: save
result.description:
Writes the open graph to a .texgraph file, so the work outlives this session; open reads it back. Takes path: .texgraph is added when the path does not end in it; a relative path resolves against patina's working directory, and the result gives the absolute path; missing folders are created; an existing file is replaced, and the result says (replaced). The file is the graph as get_graph shows it: versioned JSON, keys in one order, one node a line, so the same graph always gives the same bytes and a diff shows what changed. The path becomes the graph's path. Refused, writing nothing, while the graph has a fault: a saved graph always evaluates, but for an input node with no default, which a graph using this one as a node gives. A graph node's path resolves against the file's folder, so the graph is judged there: saved into another folder, a nested file not found from it is a fault, and one found there that differs from the file it uses now refuses the save, naming both: the saved graph is the graph defined. Only the open graph is written, never a file it uses as a graph node. The error lists the faults, each naming its node and port or parameter; fix them with edit_graph. Also refused: no open graph, an empty path, one naming a folder or holding a character a path may not, and a write that fails (naming the path and the system's message; no partial file is left). save changes nothing in the graph or the snapshot stack, which is never saved.
Worked example, after define_graph's and edit_graph's worked examples (put patina's working directory for <folder>):
save {"path":"planks"}
returns: save: saved planks.texgraph to <folder>/planks.texgraph: 6 nodes, size 256, seed 0

path.description: The file to write, absolute or relative to patina's working directory; .texgraph is added if missing.

result.name: open
result.description:
Replaces the open graph with the one in a .texgraph file (save writes them). Takes path: .texgraph is added when the path does not end in it, and a relative path resolves against patina's working directory. The file's path becomes the graph's path, and the snapshot stack is cleared. A graph node's path resolves against the file's own folder; the result names each nested file it read. A graph whose references are wrong (an input naming no node, an unknown type or parameter, a value out of range, a cycle) still opens, and the result lists its faults one a line, each naming its node and port or parameter, so edit_graph can fix them; save refuses it until they are fixed. Refused, leaving the open graph as it was: a missing file (the error lists the .texgraph files in its folder, so a misspelt name shows the right one); a file that is not a graph (not JSON, a missing or unknown key, a version other than 1, a bad size or seed), giving the line and column; an empty path, or one naming a folder.
Worked example, after save's worked example (put patina's working directory for <folder>):
open {"path":"planks.texgraph"}
returns: open: opened planks.texgraph from <folder>/planks.texgraph: 6 nodes, size 256, seed 0; no faults: it evaluates
open {"path":"plank"} is refused: open: no file at <folder>/plank.texgraph; the .texgraph files in <folder> (1) are: planks.texgraph

path.description: The .texgraph file to read, absolute or relative to patina's working directory; .texgraph is added if missing.

result.name: push_snapshot
result.description:
Copies the open graph onto a stack of snapshots, to try a change and come back: push, edit freely, then pop_snapshot restores the graph exactly as it was pushed. Takes label, optional, a name for the snapshot that pop_snapshot gives back. Returns the stack's depth. The stack lives in this session only: it is never saved, and define_graph and open clear it. The open graph and its path are unchanged. Refused when there is no open graph.
Worked example, after define_graph's worked example:
push_snapshot {"label":"before grain"}
returns: push_snapshot: pushed 'before grain'; depth 1
then edit_graph's worked example adds the grain, and pop_snapshot {} takes the graph back to before it.

label.description: Optional: a name for the snapshot, given back by pop_snapshot.

result.name: pop_snapshot
result.description:
Restores the graph on top of the snapshot stack (push_snapshot) as the open graph, byte for byte as it was pushed, and removes it from the stack. Takes nothing. Returns the snapshot's label, the new depth, and the restored graph's nodes, size, seed and faults. The graph's path is kept, so its graph nodes resolve against that path's folder (a snapshot pushed before a save into another folder is judged there, and its faults listed); nothing is written to a file. On an empty stack it is an error that says so, and changes nothing.
Worked example, after push_snapshot's: edit_graph's worked example adds the grain (6 nodes), then pop_snapshot {} returns:
pop_snapshot: restored 'before grain'; depth 0. The graph is 4 nodes, size 256, seed 0; no faults: it evaluates
and pop_snapshot {} again is refused: pop_snapshot: the snapshot stack is empty; push_snapshot first, before the change to come back from

result.name: export
result.description:
Writes the open graph's outputs as PNG files, ready for a Carve material's texture slots. Takes folder (required; absolute or relative to patina's working directory; created if missing), size (a power of two from 32 to 8192; default the graph's own size) and outputs (a list of roles from base_colour, normal, roughness, occlusion, height, and named outputs by their names; default every output the graph has). Each file is <folder>/<role>.png or <folder>/<name>.png, overwriting a file of that name (the result says replaced), written as the graph's outputs are packed for glTF: base_colour is sRGB; normal is tangent space, green up; roughness is a glTF metallic-roughness image (R 255, roughness in G, the graph's metallic in B, 0 when it has none), so define_material's metallic_roughness_texture takes it as it is; metallic has no file of its own (name roughness to write it); occlusion and height are grey; a named output is grey if greyscale, sRGB if colour. The result lists each file with its size, its bytes and the Carve material slot it belongs in: base_colour in base_colour_texture, normal in normal_texture, roughness in metallic_roughness_texture, occlusion in occlusion_texture; height and named outputs have no slot. Exporting the graph at its own size gives the same bytes every time, and equals the PNGs beside samples/graphs/planks.texgraph. Outputs are evaluated and written one at a time, in tiles, so memory stays bounded at 8192 (the planks peaked at 0.7 GB), but 8192 is slow, mostly evaluation: the planks' four outputs took 28 to 31 s in release, about 3 to 4 min in debug, each PNG 0.3 to 1 MB. A client with a short call timeout should ask for one or two outputs at a time. To look at a graph, use swatch (at 2048 or below); export is for files. Refused, writing nothing, while the graph has a fault (the error lists them; fix them with edit_graph); no open graph; a size that is not a power of two from 32 to 8192; an output the graph has not; metallic named alone; and a folder that cannot be written (the error names the folder and the system's reason).
Worked example, after open of samples/graphs/planks.texgraph (<folder> is the absolute path of textures/planks under patina's working directory):
export {"folder":"textures/planks","size":1024,"outputs":["base_colour","normal"]}
returns, a line for each file:
export: wrote 2 files to <folder> at size 1024
- base_colour.png: 1024x1024, <bytes> bytes, slot base_colour_texture
- normal.png: 1024x1024, <bytes> bytes, slot normal_texture
parameters: the graph's exposed parameters to set for this export only, by name (get_graph lists them and their ranges); the graph is not changed, the first line names them, and a value out of range is refused naming the parameter and its range, writing nothing. The files equal those of the same values set in the graph with edit_graph's set_parameters, byte for byte.
Worked example, after open of samples/graphs/bricks.texgraph: export {"folder":"textures/bricks_grey","parameters":{"mortar":0.08,"tint":"#7a7a70"}} writes its four outputs as grey stone bricks (equal to samples/graphs/bricks/variants/grey/) and its first line is:
export: wrote 4 files to <folder> at size 256, parameters mortar 0.08, tint "#7a7a70"
Worked example, after define_graph of the metal plate (nodes' output example) (<folder> is the absolute path of textures/plate):
export {"folder":"textures/plate"}
returns:
export: wrote 3 files to <folder> at size 64
- base_colour.png: 64x64, <bytes> bytes, slot base_colour_texture
- roughness.png: 64x64, <bytes> bytes, slot metallic_roughness_texture, metallic in B
- edge.png: 64x64, <bytes> bytes, no Carve slot (a named output)

folder.description: The folder to write <role>.png and <name>.png files into, absolute or relative to patina's working directory; created if missing.

size.description: A power of two from 32 to 8192; default the graph's own size.

outputs.description: The outputs to write, each a role (base_colour, normal, roughness, occlusion, height; metallic is written in roughness.png) or a named output's name; default every output the graph has.

parameters.description: Optional: the graph's exposed parameters to set for this call, by name, such as {"mortar": 0.08, "tint": "#7a7a70"}; the graph is not changed. get_graph lists them with their ranges.

result.name: swatch
result.description:
Shows the open graph's outputs as images. view: sheet (default) is one image: a column per output, the roles in role order (base_colour, normal, roughness, metallic, occlusion, height; a role the graph lacks has no column) and then the named outputs a to z, each output flat on top and tiled 3 x 3 below in 256 px cells, beside a 512 px sphere wearing base colour, normal, roughness with metallic, and occlusion (height and named outputs are shown, not worn), under a title strip with the file, size and seed. flat is one output's texels exactly, size px a side; tiled is its 3 x 3 repeat (3 x size, scaled down to at most 1536 px), to show seams; sphere is the engine's UV sphere (u once around, v from the top pole) drawn with a PBR material made of the outputs (base colour sRGB, roughness as the metallic-roughness image with the graph's metallic in B and the material's metallic factor 1, or metallic 0 when the graph has none, normal and occlusion linear, mipmaps on; a missing role uses the material's default), lit as Carve's render lights a model, on Carve's dark slate, from a fixed camera, 512 px. metallic, height and greyscale named outputs are drawn grey; roughness's column is roughness alone. output: a role or a named output's name, for flat and tiled (default the first role the graph has). size: the evaluation size, a power of two from 32 to 2048 (default the graph's size, at most 2048; for larger PNGs use export). cube is a lit cube (edge 0.7, each face its own UVs 0 to 1, u to the right and v down as the face is seen) wearing the same material, turned so the front, the left and the top show, to judge a material on flat faces and the edges between them; lit and framed as the sphere is, 512 px. tiling: a whole number from 1 to 8 (default 1), for sheet, sphere and cube: the sphere or cube wears every map repeated that many times in u and v, to judge a material at a texel density nearer a game's; the sheet's title and the result name it when it is not 1. angle: the sphere's or cube's turn about y in degrees, for sheet, sphere and cube (default 0; counter-clockwise seen from above). parameters: the graph's exposed parameters to set for this call only, by name (get_graph lists them and their ranges); the graph is not changed, a value out of range is refused, and the sheet's title and the result name them. Refused while the graph has a fault. Changes nothing.
Worked examples, with samples/graphs/planks.texgraph open, each returning an image and a line: swatch {"view":"tiled","output":"base_colour","size":128} returns:
swatch tiled: base_colour of planks.texgraph, 3 x 3 of 128 px, 384 x 384 px, exact texels
swatch {"view":"cube","tiling":3} returns:
swatch cube: planks.texgraph at 256 px on a cube, each face 0 to 1 in u and v, angle 0, tiling 3, 512 x 512 px
swatch {"view":"sphere","tiling":3} returns:
swatch sphere: planks.texgraph at 256 px on the engine's UV sphere, angle 0, tiling 3, 512 x 512 px
After define_graph of the metal plate (nodes' output example): swatch {"view":"flat","output":"edge"} returns an image and:
swatch flat: edge of the open graph, 64 x 64 px, exact texels
With samples/graphs/bricks.texgraph open: swatch {"view":"flat","output":"base_colour","parameters":{"mortar":0.08,"tint":"#7a7a70"}} shows grey stone bricks' base colour and returns:
swatch flat: base_colour of bricks.texgraph, 256 x 256 px, exact texels; parameters mortar 0.08, tint "#7a7a70"
and swatch {"parameters":{"mortar":0.5}} returns:
swatch: parameters['mortar']: is 0.5, but must be a number from 0 to 0.45
and swatch {"view":"sphere","tiling":9} returns:
swatch: tiling 9 is out of range; give a whole number from 1 to 8

output.description: A role (base_colour, normal, roughness, metallic, occlusion, height) or a named output's name, for flat and tiled.

tiling.description: Whole repeats of every map over the sphere or cube in u and v, 1 to 8 (default 1), for sheet, sphere and cube.

parameters.description: Optional: the graph's exposed parameters to set for this call, by name, such as {"mortar": 0.08, "tint": "#7a7a70"}; the graph is not changed. get_graph lists them with their ranges.

result.name: check
result.description:
Measures the open graph's outputs as numbers, rather than judging by a render, and lists what is wrong with each, with the fix in words. Changes nothing, and never refuses a graph that evaluates: a fault is a problem in the list. Takes size (a power of two from 32 to 2048; default the graph's own, at most 2048), parameters (the graph's exposed parameters, for this call only) and files (a list of {path, role} of PNGs, the path absolute or relative to patina's working directory; only those are checked, no graph is needed, and size and parameters are not used). Role metallic_roughness is a packed image as export writes roughness.png (G roughness, B metallic); role roughness is roughness only. The rules, each with its thresholds and what it means for a game:
- base-colour-range: base colour's brightest channel, in sRGB levels 0 to 255, should be 20 to 245 for a non-metal texel (metallic below 0.5, or no metallic) and 120 or more for a metal texel (metallic 0.5 or more); near black is a hole under game lighting, near white blows out, and dark metal, which takes its colour from reflection, shows almost nothing. A fault when over 1% of texels are out. Fix: pull the darks up and the lights in with a levels or gradient_map node.
- metallic-not-binary: metallic should be 0 or 1, with a sharp edge between (a half-metal is not a real surface and renders as dull chrome). A fault when over 5% of texels are from 0.1 to 0.9. Fix: push the mask to 0 and 1 (a levels node with in_low equal to in_high is a step), or set a constant.
- normal-not-unit: a normal is a unit vector. A fault when over 0.1% of texels' length differs from 1 by more than 0.02 (0.03 for a PNG, for the 8-bit rounding). Fix: make it with height_to_normal, which normalises, and do not mix a normal's components as colours.
- one-value: a greyscale output (roughness, occlusion, height, a greyscale named output; not metallic) whose texels all pack to one byte; a mask of one value masks nothing. Fix: widen its levels, or drive it from a noise or pattern, or drop the output.
- does-not-tile: the mean step between neighbouring columns (and rows, for v), in packed levels over the channels, is measured at every column boundary, the wrap's between the last and first included; the wrap is a fault when its step is more than twice the 99th percentile of the steps inside, plus 2 levels, so the texture shows a seam when it repeats (a pattern's own hard edge that falls on the wrap is not one). Fix: whole-number frequencies and counts and quarter turns; swatch's tiled view shows where.
Result: {ok, problems:[{check, output, message}], notes, stats}. ok is true when there are no problems; each message gives the share, the worst texel and the fix; notes say how the texels were read (the share of metal texels, a metallic read from a packed file); stats gives each output's min, max and mean per channel, in packed levels 0 to 255 (a normal's too: 127.5 is zero), at stats.size (mixed-size files: each output's width and height). Errors, writing nothing: no open graph (when no files are given), a graph with a fault (the error lists them; fix them with edit_graph), a size that is not allowed, a parameter that is refused, and a file that is missing or not a PNG.
Worked example, with samples/graphs/bricks.texgraph open: check {"size":64} returns, clean:
{"ok":true,"problems":[],"notes":[],"stats":{"size":64,"outputs":{"base_colour":{"min":[108,45,30],"max":[194,186,169],"mean":[160.3,104.4,86.5]},"normal":{"min":[72,72,242],"max":[183,183,255],"mean":[127.9,127.7,250.3]},"roughness":{"min":[167],"max":[255],"mean":[202.6]},"occlusion":{"min":[115],"max":[255],"mean":[183.6]}}}}

size.description: A power of two from 32 to 2048; default the graph's own size (at most 2048).
